name: update-task-into-argued-partition
description: A task re-pointed into a partition whose argument already stood. The argument answered nothing while the partition ran one level; the move makes it mixed, so the standing text starts answering `safety.component-below-partition` without a single edit to it — the argument GOING LIVE, asked about as a declaration is.

context.summary: The `examples/basic` model with `ExampleSWC` declaring D and `ExampleConsumerSWC` deriving `QM`, `Task_10ms` running both with its own execution-time argument in the unrated `PARTITION0`, and `PARTITION1` on `CORE0` rated D, argued and running nothing; the baseline reports nothing. The change set moves the task into `PARTITION1`.

authorization.notes: The scope covers the address exactly, and it is a TASK's field: the delta touches no hardware element at all. The guard compares the two models, sees `PARTITION1` become mixed under a text that already stood, and asks `declare_partition_coexistence` once, which is why the status is `committed`.

input.intent: Run the mixed task in PARTITION1.

expected.notes: `committed` after the second question. Re-pointing a task is otherwise a placement change pass D re-judges and the guard does not ask about; it asks here because the move made a standing argument answer a finding, which is the one condition the rule can see.
